answer: Each identity locks 80 credits in a haven and posts one key-signed checkpoint per epoch hashing the prior checkpoint plus work, forming one chain. An auditor recomputes the hashes in the atlas; a missing link or second branch from the same key breaks the chain and burns the 80 bond. Each checkpoint docks at an epoch jetty. The kth fake needs its own 80 bond and chain, so 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 and pay 15,000 in fees. A chain-rental ring fails: a borrowed checkpoint hashes to a different key and atlas entry. An honest agent pays 80 once and recovers it after a clean epoch.
